title: Comparing Ambiguous and Stratified Grammar Trees
description: Build binary AST dictionaries with op, val, left, and right keys to compare ambiguous and layered parse trees for 2 + 3 * 4 and 5 - 2 - 1.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `leaf(v)` and `node(op, l, r)` construct binary tree dictionaries with keys `"op"`, `"val"`, `"left"`, and `"right"`. `pretty` prints internal nodes as `({t['op']})` with indented children, and `evaluate` recurses on `t["left"]` and `t["right"]` before applying `t["op"]`.

Lines 37-38 construct both trees permitted by an ambiguous flat grammar for `2 + 3 * 4`. `ambig_tree_A` has `"+"` at the root (`14`), and `ambig_tree_B` has `"*"` at the root (`20`). Line 42 constructs `unambig_tree`, the single tree permitted by the layered `E/T/F` grammar.

Notice how `unambig_tree` on line 42 is identical to `ambig_tree_A` on line 37. Stratifying the grammar into `E -> E + T | T` and `T -> T * F | F` eliminates `ambig_tree_B`. Only `node("+", leaf(2), node("*", leaf(3), leaf(4)))` can be derived.

steps.question: In `left_assoc` (line 60) and `right_assoc` (line 61), which sub-subtraction runs first inside `evaluate` for each tree, and what two values do lines 62-63 print?
steps.answer: In `left_assoc`, the left child `node("-", leaf(5), leaf(2))` evaluates to `3` first and `3 - 1` prints `2`. In `right_assoc`, the right child `node("-", leaf(2), leaf(1))` evaluates to `1` first and `5 - 1` prints `4`.

steps.description: Inside `evaluate(ambig_tree_A)`, the right subtree `node('*', leaf(3), leaf(4))` computes `l * r` (`3 * 4 = 12`) on line 27. The root `'+'` then adds `2`.
